documents.text:
March 12, 2026

The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
Secretary
Federal Energy Regulatory Commission
888 First St., N.E.
Washington D.C. 20426

Re:    Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Docket No. ER26-____-000
       Submission of Tariff Revisions to Attachment Z1 to Limit Long-Term Service to
       Interconnection Service Amount

Dear Secretary Reese:

       Pursuant to Section 205 of the Federal Power Act (“FPA”), 16 U.S.C. § 824d, and
Section 35.13 of the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission’s (“Commission”)
Regulations, 18 C.F.R. § 35.13, Southwest Power Pool, Inc. (“SPP”) submits revisions to
Attachment Z1 of the SPP Open Access Transmission Tariff (“Tariff”) 1 to provide




1
       Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Open Access Transmission Tariff, Sixth Revised
       Volume No. 1. References in this filing to "Tariff" refer to the version of SPP’s
       Tariff currently in effect. "Proposed Tariff" refers to a version reflecting the
       revisions proposed in this filing. All capitalized terms not otherwise defined in this
       filing shall have the definitions assigned by the Tariff.
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
March 12, 2026
Page 2


Eligible Customers 2 with flexibility to procure Long-Term Service 3 through the
Aggregate Transmission Service Study 4 (“ATSS”) process while seeking generator
interconnection service through the applicable generator interconnection process.

        SPP respectfully requests that the Commission accept the proposed revisions, find
the revisions just and reasonable, and set an effective date of May 12, 2026, which is at
least sixty (60) days after filing.

I.     BACKGROUND

A.     SPP

       SPP is a Commission-approved Regional Transmission Organization (“RTO”). 5 It
is an Arkansas non-profit corporation with its principal place of business in Little Rock,
Arkansas. SPP currently has 139 members, including 16 investor-owned utilities, 13
municipal systems, 25 generation and transmission cooperatives, 6 state agencies, 27
independent power producers, 11 power marketers, 16 independent transmission

2
       Tariff, Part I, Section 1, Definition of Eligible Customer (“(i) Any electric utility
       (including the Transmission Owner(s) and any power marketer), Federal Power
       Marketing Agency, or any person generating electric energy for sale for
       resale. Electric energy sold or produced by such entity may be electric energy
       produced in the United States, Canada or Mexico. However, with respect to
       transmission service that the Commission is prohibited from ordering by Section
       212(h) of the Federal Power Act, such entity is eligible only if the service is
       provided pursuant to a state requirement that a Transmission Owner offer the
       unbundled transmission service, or pursuant to a voluntary offer of such service
       by a Transmission Owner. (ii) Any retail customer or eligible person taking
       unbundled transmission service pursuant to a state requirement that a
       Transmission Owner offer the transmission service, or pursuant to a voluntary
       offer of such service by a Transmission Owner, is an Eligible Customer under the
       Tariff.”).
3
       Id., Definition of Long-Term Service (“Long-Term Firm Point-To-Point
       Transmission Service or Network Integration Transmission Service of one year or
       longer.”).
4
       Id., Definition of Aggregate Transmission Service Study (“Transmission facilities
       studies as described in Attachment Z1 that aggregate Transmission Service
       requests received over an open season. These requests are evaluated
       simultaneously to provide for optimization of transmission expansion.”).
5
       See Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 109 FERC ¶ 61,009 (2004), order on reh’g, 110 FERC
       ¶ 61,137 (2005).
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
March 12, 2026
Page 3


companies, 1 federal agency, 13 large retail customers, 4 alternative power entities, and 7
public interest entities. As an RTO, SPP: (1) administers, across the facilities of SPP's
Transmission Owners, open access transmission service over approximately 72,000 miles
of transmission lines covering portions of Arkansas, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Minnesota,
Missouri, Montana, Nebraska, New Mexico, North Dakota, Oklahoma, South Dakota,
Texas, and Wyoming; and (2) administers the Integrated Marketplace, a centralized day-
ahead and real-time Energy and Operating Reserve market with locational marginal
pricing and market-based congestion management. 6

B.     Stakeholder Approval

       The revisions proposed herein were reviewed and approved through the SPP
stakeholder process, including meetings of: the Transmission Working Group (“TWG”)
on September 30, 2025; 7 the Cost Allocation Working Group (“CAWG”) on November
14, 2025 (unanimously); 8 the Regional Tariff Working Group (“RTWG”) on November
20, 2025; 9 and the Markets and Operations Policy Committee (“MOPC”) on January 13-


6
       See Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 146 FERC ¶ 61,130 (2014) (order approving the start-
       up and operation of the Integrated Marketplace effective March 1, 2014).
7
       See TWG Meeting Minutes, dated September 30, 2025, at Agenda Item 8, posted
       at:
       https://spp.org/documents/74957/twg%20meeting%20minutes%2020250930.pdf
       . The TWG develops and oversees regional and interregional transmission
       planning processes, including generator interconnection and long-term
       transmission service study processes. The TWG reviews proposed transmission
       interconnections and coordinates transmission planning activities to develop
       SPP’s Integrated Transmission Plan and Transmission Expansion Plan.
8
       See CAWG Meeting Minutes, dated November 14, 2025, at Agenda Item 2, posted
       at: https://spp.org/documents/75316/cawg%20minutes%2020251114.pdf . The
       CAWG reports to the Regional State Committee (RSC) and assists the RSC in
       addressing matters for which the RSC has primary responsibility as defined in
       Section 7.2 of the SPP Bylaws. In addition, the CAWG assists the RSC in
       addressing any other issues as requested by the RSC.
9
       See RTWG Meeting Minutes, dated November 20, 2025, at Agenda Item 9, posted
       at:
       https://spp.org/documents/75390/rtwg%20meeting%20minutes%2020251120.pd
       f. The RTWG develops, implements and oversees SPP’s Open Access
       Transmission Tariff. The RTWG provides input on regulatory or implementation
       issues not specifically covered by the rariff and issues where there may be
       conflicting or differing interpretations of the tariff.
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
March 12, 2026
Page 4


14, 2026. 10 While SPP recognizes that stakeholder approval does not by itself cause a
filing to be just and reasonable, SPP requests that the Commission extend appropriate
deference to the wishes of SPP’s stakeholders, consistent with Commission precedent. 11

II.    PURPOSE AND JUSTIFICATION FOR THE PROPOSED TARIFF
       REVISIONS

         Attachment Z1 of the Tariff describes the ATSS process used to evaluate Long-
Term Service requests. 12 Under the ATSS process, SPP combines all Long-Term Service
requests during a specified period of time (“open season”) into a single ATSS, apart from
certain requests that meet exemption requirements described in Section 30.2.2 of the
Tariff. 13 Combining all requests received during an open season allows SPP to develop a




10
       See MOPC Meeting Minutes, dated January 13-14, 2026, at Agenda Item 5, posted
       at:
       https://spp.org/documents/75745/mopc%20meeting%20minutes%20and%20ball
       ots_20260113_combined%20file.pdf. The MOPC consists of a representative
       officer or employee from each SPP Member and reports to the SPP Board of
       Directors. Its responsibilities include recommending modifications to the tariff.
       See Southwest Power Pool, Inc., Bylaws, First Revised Volume No. 4 ("Bylaws")
       at Section 6.1.
11
       The Commission has previously recognized that provisions approved through
       RTO stakeholder processes are due deference. See Sw. Power Pool, Inc., 127
       FERC ¶ 61,283, at P 33 (2009) (noting that the Commission "accord[s] an
       appropriate degree of deference to RTO stakeholder processes"); New Eng. Power
       Pool, 105 FERC ¶ 61,300, at P 34 (2003) (Commission approval of transmission
       cost allocation proposal based upon an extensive and thorough stakeholder
       process); Policy Statement Regarding Regional Transmission Groups, 1991-1996
       FERC Stats. & Regs., Preambles ¶ 30,976, at 30,872 (1993) (the Commission will
       afford the appropriate degree of deference to the stakeholder approval process).
       The Commission’s deference to RTO stakeholder processes has been upheld by
       the courts. See Pub. Serv. Comm’n of Wis. v. FERC, 545 F.3d 1058, 1062-63 (D.C.
       Cir. 2008) (noting the Commission often gives weight to RTO proposals that
       reflect the position of the majority of the RTO’s stakeholders) (quoting Am. Elec.
       Power Serv. Corp. v. Midwest Indep. Transmission Sys. Operator, Inc., 122 FERC
       ¶ 61,083, at P 172 (2008)).
12
       Tariff, Attachment Z1, Section I.
13
       Id.
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
March 12, 2026
Page 5


more efficient expansion of the Transmission System 14 that provides the necessary
Available Transfer Capability to accommodate all such requests at the minimum total cost.

        Section II of Attachment Z1 of the Tariff describes the open season period, during
which an Eligible Customer may request Long-Term Firm Point-To-Point Transmission
Service 15 or Network Integration Transmission Service 16 (NITS) of one year or longer by
submitting a Completed Application that includes all of the information specified under
Sections 17.2 and 17.3 or 17.8 for Long-Term Firm Point-To-Point requests and Section
29.2 for NITS requests. 17 Business Practice 7500, in place since July 2022, expands on
the Tariff’s requirements for the ATSS and limits the amount of Long-Term Service an
Eligible Customer may request from a specific point of interconnection (POI) to the
injection limit at the POI as determined by the Generator Interconnection Agreement(s)
(“GIA(s)”) associated with the POI. 18 Business Practice 7500 allows SPP to reject any
Long-Term Service request submitted into the ATSS process from sources at the same
POI, which result in existing plus requested transmission service to exceed the GIA
interconnection service amount at the POI. 19 The purpose of this limitation is to minimize

14

       III and Part IV of the Tariff.”).
15
       Id., Definition of Long-Term Firm Point-To-Point Transmission Service (“Firm
       Point-To-Point Transmission Service under Part II of the Tariff with a term of one
       year or more.”).
16
       Id., Definition of Network Integration Transmission Service (“The transmission
       service provided under Part III of the Tariff.”).
17

18

       at Business Practice 7500 posted at: https://www.spp.org/spp-documents-
       filings/?id=18162 (“Business Practices”).
19
       Id.; see also Order No. 890 at P 245 (“We agree…that inclusion of all requests for
       transmission service in ETC (Existing Transmission Commitments) would likely
       overstate usage of the system and understate ATC. We therefore find that
       reservations that have the same point of receipt (POR) (generator) but different
       point of delivery (POD) (load), for the same time frame, should not be modeled in
       the ETC calculation simultaneously if their combined reserved transmission
       capacity exceeds the generator’s nameplate capacity at the POR. This will prevent
       overly unrealistic utilization of transmission capacity associated with power output
       from a generator identified as a POR. We direct public utilities, working through
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
March 12, 2026
Page 6


the risk of overselling system capacity which could lead to unnecessary congestion and
curtailment of service. Furthermore, it allows an Eligible Customer to seek Long-Term
Service and interconnection service simultaneously, thereby facilitating load additions
and optimizing transmission usage.

       SPP seeks to put the language in Business Practice 7500, described above, into
Attachment Z1 of the Tariff. SPP believes this language affects the rates, terms, and
conditions of SPP transmission service and, therefore, should be documented in the Tariff
and made a part of the filed rate. The Proposed Tariff is just and reasonable and not unduly
preferential or discriminatory because it allows SPP to manage and protect system
capacity while offering Eligible Customers the flexibility to procure Long-Term Service
through the ATSS while simultaneously seeking Generator Interconnection Service. 20 The
added flexibility will benefit Eligible Customers seeking service through both processes
and will benefit SPP stakeholders and the footprint as a whole by facilitating load
additions and optimizing transmission usage while minimizing the risk of overselling
system capacity. The Commission should accept the Proposed Tariff, as described herein.

III.   DESCRIPTION OF             THE      SPECIFIC         TARIFF    CHANGES           AND
       JUSTIFICATION

       A.      Part I, Section 1 Definitions P

       SPP proposes to add the following definition to Part I, Section of the Tariff:

       Point of Interconnection: A physical location, as set forth in Appendix A to the
       Generator Interconnection Agreement, Interim Generator Interconnection
       Agreement, or Consolidated Planning Process Generator Interconnection
       Agreement (CPP GIA), as applicable, where the Interconnection Facilities
       connect to the Transmission System. 21



       NERC, to develop requirements in MOD-001 that lay out clear instructions on
       how these reservations should be accounted.”); see also Order No. 2003-A at P
       535 (“Although obtaining Interconnection Service under this rule and obtaining
       transmission delivery service under the OATT is a two-step process, the
       Interconnection Customer has every right to request the two services at the same
       time, just as it did in the past.”).
20
       Tariff, Part 1, Section 1, Definition of Generator Interconnection Service (“Shall
       be as defined as “Interconnection Service” as applicable in Attachment V or
       AY.”).
21
       Proposed Tariff, Part I, Section 1, Definitions P.
 The Honorable Debbie-Anne A. Reese
March 12, 2026
Page 7


       The language in Section VII of Attachment Z1 of the Proposed Tariff describes
resource limitations at the POI, making a definition of POI in Part I, Section 1 of the Tariff
necessary.

B.     Attachment Z1, Section VII

        SPP proposes adding a new Section VII to Attachment Z1 of the Proposed Tariff
for POI resource limitations. This new section will allow an Eligible Customer to request
Long-Term Service from resource(s) that represent a single or multiple POIs up to the
interconnection limit at the POI(s). 22 SPP will look to the applicable GIA, Interim GIA,
or CPP GIA to determine the interconnection limit at the POI. 23 The proposed section also
allows the Transmission Provider to refuse a Long-Term Service request submitted into
the ATSS that results in existing transmission service plus the requested transmission
service exceeding the interconnection limit at the POI stated in the applicable GIA. 24

III.   EFFECTIVE DATE

        For all the reasons discussed in this transmittal letter, SPP requests that the
Commission accept the proposed revisions to the Tariff to become effective May 12, 2026,
which is not less than 60 days or more than 120 days prior to the submission of this filing
as required by the Commission. 25

IV.    ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

       A.      Information Provided Per Commission Regulations

               1.      Documents submitted with this filing:

                       In addition to this Transmittal Letter, Clean and Redlined Tariff
                       revisions under the Sixth Revised Volume No. 1.

               2.      Service:

                       SPP has electronically served a copy of this filing on all its
                       Members, Transmission Customers and Market Participants. A
                       complete copy of this filing will be posted on the SPP website,

                       www.spp.org and is also being served on all affected state
                       commissions.

               3.      Requisite agreements:

                       Not applicable.

       B.      Communications

       Correspondence and communications with respect to this filing should be sent to,
       and SPP asks the Secretary to include on the official service list, the following:

        Tessie Kentner                        Meredith Powell
        Director & Associate General          Attorney
        Counsel                               Southwest Power Pool, Inc.

V.     CONCLUSION

       For all of the foregoing reasons, SPP respectfully requests that the Commission
accept the Tariff revisions proposed herein as just and reasonable and not unduly
discriminatory or preferential, to be effective May 12, 2026, which is not less than 60 days
or more than 120 days prior to the submission of this filing.

P - Definitions


       Part I: Tariff Definitions and Common Service Provisions contained in Sections 2
       through 12.


       Part II:      Tariff Sections 13 through 27 pertaining to Point-To-Point Transmission
       Service in conjunction with the applicable Common Service Provisions of Part I and
       appropriate Schedules and Attachments.


       Part III: Tariff Sections 28 through 36 pertaining to Network Integration Transmission
       Service in conjunction with the applicable Common Service Provisions of Part I and
       appropriate Schedules and Attachments.


       Part IV: Tariff Sections 37 through 39 pertaining to special Tariff provisions related to
       the applicability of the Tariff during and after the Transition Period and special Tariff
       provisions related to participation by the United States.


       Part V:       Tariff Sections 40 through 42, and related Schedules and Attachments,
       pertaining to recovery of costs for Base Plan Upgrades and approved Balanced Portfolios.


       Parties: The Transmission Provider and the Transmission Customer receiving service
       under the Tariff.


       Point(s) of Delivery: Point(s) on the Transmission Provider's Transmission System
       where capacity and energy transmitted by the Transmission Provider will be made
       available to the Receiving Party under Part II and Part III of the Tariff. The Point(s) of
       Delivery shall be specified in the Service Agreement for Long-Term Firm Point-To-Point
       Transmission Service.


       Point of Interconnection: A physical location, as set forth in Appendix A to the
       Generator Interconnection Agreement, Interim Generator Interconnection Agreement, or
 Consolidated Planning Process Generator Interconnection Agreement (CPP GIA), as
applicable, where the Interconnection Facilities connect to the Transmission System.


Point(s) of Receipt:      Point(s) of interconnection on the Transmission Provider's
Transmission System where capacity and/or energy will be made available to the
Transmission Provider by the Delivering Party under Part II and Part III of the Tariff.
The Point(s) of Receipt shall be specified in the Service Agreement for Long-Term Firm
Point-To-Point Transmission Service.


Point-To-Point Transmission Service: The reservation and transmission of capacity
and energy on either a firm or non-firm basis from the Point(s) of Receipt to the Point(s)
of Delivery under Part II of the Tariff.


Power Purchaser:        The entity that is purchasing the capacity and energy to be
transmitted under the Tariff.


Pre-Confirmed Application: An Application that commits the Eligible Customer to
execute a Service Agreement upon receipt of notification that the Transmission Provider
can provide the requested Transmission Service.


Project Sponsor: One or more entities that voluntarily agree to bear a portion or all of
the costs of a Sponsored Upgrade.


Provisional Load Process: This process, as described in Attachment AX of the Tariff,
allows the Transmission Provider to assess the request for delivery point additions or
changes when the Transmission Customer does not have enough existing Designated
Resources to serve the increased load plus losses.


Provisional Load Process Agreement: The agreements found in Addendum 2 and
Addendum 3 of Attachment AX of the Tariff, and any amendments or supplements
 thereto, entered into by the Eligible Transmission Customer and the Transmission
Provider.


Public Policy Requirements: Requirements established by local, state or federal laws or
regulations, including duly enacted statutes or regulations promulgated by a relevant
jurisdiction, whether within a state, or at the federal level.
 VII.   Transmission Service Limit
A.     Point of Interconnection Resource Limitations
An Eligible Customer may request Long-Term Service from resource(s) that represents a single
or multiple Point of Interconnection(s) up to the interconnection limit at the Point of
Interconnection(s). Any such Long-Term Service requests submitted into the Aggregate
Transmission Service Study process which result in existing transmission service plus requested
transmission service to be more than the interconnection limit at the Point of Interconnection(s)
will be refused by the Transmission Provider in OASIS.
